how_to_read: Requirement status is recomputed from repository artifacts by `requirements/scripts/req_site.py`, not typed in by hand. Codes: MET = an artifact exists AND its verification passed in this session; PARTIAL = artifact exists but a named evidence gate is still missing; NOT MET = no artifact, and the reason is recorded; NOT POSSIBLE = the requirement cannot be satisfied from official sources at all, with the reason recorded. 'Evidence' links only ever point at official NFL/standards-body pages or at this repository's own check output; the repository is never cited as proof that an NFL fact is true.
summary_rule: A requirement is never marked MET on the strength of a build passing. Build success is a software check; MET requires the underlying evidence, and where the evidence is a third-party number the requirement stays NOT MET by design. Every requirement row also carries the official page that its evidence rests on.

requirements.source_quote: "The goal of this project is to collect, organize, and analyze utilizing a full list of requirements."
requirements.requirement: Every operator requirement is enumerated, individually tracked, and traceable to the artifact that satisfies it or the reason it is unmet.
requirements.what_exists: 16 requirement rows below, each with a source quote, an artifact path and a computed status; the status is produced by requirements/scripts/req_site.py from the artifacts themselves.
requirements.review: RQ-01 is self-referential: it is only MET because a reviewer can read this table. No external source is involved.

requirements.source_quote: "Make suggestions on how to improve the site to improve decision making and create a section dedicated for suggestions so someone can review suggestions and choose the best path before implementing any changes."
requirements.requirement: A dedicated Suggestions section, each suggestion reviewable with options, cost, risk, evidence and an explicit decision state, and nothing implemented before a decision is recorded.
requirements.what_exists: 16 suggestions, each with options A/B/C, what it would cost, risk, the evidence that would justify it, and a decision field that is currently UNDECIDED for every row. Suggestion SG-15 records decisions already taken inside this session so nothing is implemented invisibly.
requirements.what_is_missing: An operator decision on each row. The reviewing human is the only actor who can move a row out of UNDECIDED; the session deliberately did not pick for them.
requirements.review: Whether the decision states satisfy the operator is a judgement call that this session cannot verify.

requirements.source_quote: "I want a clear list of questions, informations and answers that need to be addressed before any decision can be reasonably made bases upon the information that we already have and do not have. Suggestions need to be made to discover missing information."
requirements.requirement: An open-question register that states, per question, what we have, what we lack, what would answer it, and how to obtain the missing information.
requirements.what_exists: 22 questions (Q-01 to Q-22). Every row carries: what we already have with a source link, what we lack, the exact official page or action that would resolve it, and the decision it blocks. Of those, 12 are ANSWERED from official sources inside this session, 7 remain OPEN, 2 are marked IMPOSSIBLE because no official source can answer them, and 1 is partial.
requirements.what_is_missing: The OPEN rows depend on data that no official NFL page publishes (depth-chart order, sportsbook prices, closing lines) or on time (a settled forecast ledger). The register states each dependency rather than guessing around it.
requirements.review: The 'what would resolve it' column names a page or an action; it does not guarantee the page stays available or that the action is permitted.

requirements.source_quote: "I want to originate my own NFL lines."
requirements.requirement: Own originated lines, produced from official data with no market input, for a game slate that had not yet been played.
requirements.evidence: requirements/results/week10-lines.json + requirements/pages/lines.html; method reimplemented in requirements/scripts/verify_capture.py
requirements.what_exists: 13 Week 10 fair numbers (spread and total) for the games not yet played as of 2026-11-14, built from the 137-game official log: home projection 24.06 + (home PF/G - away PA/G)/2 - (away PF/G - home PA/G)/2 style B0 rates, sigma_margin 13.1768 from the same log, plus an independent Elo cross-check. All 13 are labelled UNVALIDATED - DERIVED.
requirements.what_is_missing: Calibration against outcomes (the games are in the future) and a market comparison (no official sportsbook source exists). No line is presented as a fair price or a recommendation.
requirements.review: These numbers are this project's own arithmetic on official inputs. They are not official NFL lines and the NFL publishes no point spreads at all.

requirements.source_quote: "Research and develop strategies for generating useful signals."
requirements.requirement: Documented signal families with a pre-specified test, not just names of ideas.
requirements.evidence: origination/results/leaderboard.json (12 strategies, 8 gates) + analysis/strategies.json (8 root strategies) + requirements/pages/strategies.html
requirements.what_exists: 20 registered candidate signal families across two inherited registries (12 in origination/, 8 at root), each with a testable hypothesis, a pre-registered gate set and a recorded result. All 20 remain BLOCKED; 0 passed.
requirements.what_is_missing: The only families with a measurable out-of-sample result are the point-spread and total families graded in requirements/results/w9-grading.json, and n=15 is too small to establish skill. Player-prop and parlay families have no settled joint-outcome ledger, so they cannot be scored at all.
requirements.review: Two registries with different definitions coexist. Unifying them is suggestion SG-02 and needs an operator decision; this session did not silently pick one.

requirements.source_quote: "Treat it as a leaderboard competition that provides rewards for top performing strategies."
requirements.requirement: A leaderboard with a pre-registered reward rule that cannot be gamed by a lucky backtest.
requirements.what_exists: The rule is written and is deliberately conservative: rank only strategies that pass all eight gates, then order by the LOWER 95% confidence bound of the skill score, and award paper points only. Because 0 of 20 strategies pass a gate, the leaderboard has no medals, no ranks and no rewards, and every reward cell is blank by design.
requirements.what_is_missing: At least one strategy that clears the gates. That needs many more settled forecasts, which needs a pre-kickoff forecast ledger that does not exist yet.
requirements.review: The reward rule is this project's design, not an official NFL or regulator rule. No cash reward is implemented or implied.

requirements.source_quote: "Look at single bet, parlays, player prop bet combos."
requirements.requirement: All three product families covered, with the joint-event mathematics made explicit for parlay and prop combinations.
requirements.what_exists: Singles have an actual out-of-sample grade (15 Week 9 games). Parlay and prop combinations are covered as a stated method: joint probability P(A and B) = pA*pB + rho*sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)), which is only usable with a measured rho. The correlation register publishes the measured rho values that do exist and leaves the rest blank.
requirements.what_is_missing: A player-level, event-aligned dataset: same player, same game, same threshold, same pregame timestamp. Without it, no rho can be estimated and no combo can be priced. The repo contains no player game log, so every combo cell is blank and flagged.
requirements.review: The formula is standard probability algebra; it does not by itself validate any parlay. Quoting it is not evidence of an edge.

requirements.requirement: Explicit gates, applied fail-closed, where missing evidence can never count as a pass.
requirements.evidence: origination/results/leaderboard.json (G1..G8 fixed before results) + analysis/validation-gates.json + requirements/pages/gates.html
requirements.what_exists: Eight gates, each with its rule and current status, plus the recorded outcome 0 of 20 strategies eligible. The gates cover official-data provenance, no look-ahead, sample size, skill against a baseline, multiplicity, stability, calibration and the absence of market data.
requirements.what_is_missing: Nothing procedural. The gates are not failing because they are mis-specified; they are failing because the evidence does not exist.
requirements.review: The gate thresholds are this project's choices. They are not endorsed by the NFL or by any standards body, and the reference pages cited next to them explain the underlying statistics rather than certifying these values.

requirements.requirement: Correlation values, with the unit of observation and the sample size stated, and unmeasured pairs left blank.
requirements.what_exists: Measured values exist at team level and are reported with n, method and a classification: for example quarterback passing yards against game total, and a same-game side-versus-total residual estimate. Values that did not survive a multiplicity correction are shown with their raw and adjusted p-values rather than being dropped.
requirements.what_is_missing: Leg-level dependence for parlays and prop combos. Team aggregates cannot be used to price a combination, so those cells stay blank. Two Next Gen Stats weeks are incomplete and are flagged rather than filled.
requirements.review: Descriptive association between team aggregates is not causation and is not a betting correlation. The pages say so on every affected table.

requirements.source_quote: "Remove luck from the equation and build strategies that are selectively skill based."
requirements.requirement: Separate measured skill from luck as far as is statistically possible, and state plainly what cannot be removed.
requirements.what_exists: A quantified decomposition on official data: the share of team win-percentage variance attributable to point differential, a per-team luck residual, and confidence intervals on every rate. The measured result is stated even though it is unflattering: on the rated sample the majority of win-percentage spread is not separable from noise.
requirements.what_is_missing: The requirement as literally worded. Luck cannot be removed from a finite sample; it can only be bounded, and a bound needs many more observations than 15 games or one season. The project therefore re-scopes the requirement to 'shrink toward a conservative bound and refuse to award on an unproven point estimate', which the reward rule does.
requirements.review: This row is deliberately NOT marked MET. Marking it MET would require a claim that no statistician would support.

requirements.requirement: An injury tracker sourced from the official NFL report, with practice status and game status kept distinct.
requirements.what_exists: 345 rows covering all 28 clubs playing in Week 10, transcribed from all eight rendered chunks of the official report. Practice participation and game status are separate columns; a blank game status stays blank and is never upgraded to 'healthy'.
requirements.what_is_missing: Final inactives for the Sunday and Monday games, which the NFL publishes later. The report is a dated snapshot and is labelled as one.
requirements.review: Only practice and game status are transcribed. Nothing here is medical advice, and a 'Questionable' tag is not a probability.

requirements.source_quote: "know any deficiencies in defenses such as 2nd,3rd or 4th string backups having to replace starters due to lineups. Also same can be said for offenses using starters or backups."
requirements.requirement: Identify when a backup, not a starter, is playing, on both sides of the ball.
requirements.what_exists: A documented, tested finding that the official depth-chart URL returns HTTP 404 (the page prints '404 - Flag on the Play.'), that official roster pages publish only a status code such as ACT, and that the only official page naming a game's actual starters is the NFL Game Book PDF, one per game. The mechanism is demonstrated on one real game: the Game Book for JAX at BAL lists 12 J.Fagnano in the Ravens' quarterback slot, and Lamar Jackson appears nowhere in that game's lineups or substitutions. The NFL's own news page separately records that Jackson was placed on injured reserve.
requirements.what_is_missing: A starter designation the NFL publishes before kickoff. It does not exist on nfl.com, so a pregame 'this is a 3rd-string tackle' label cannot be produced from an official source. Any such label would have to be inferred, which this project's no-inference rule forbids.
requirements.review: The requirement is therefore split into what is possible (post-game starter confirmation from game books; injury-driven absence lists transcribed exactly) and what is impossible (a pregame depth-chart label), and the impossible half is not faked.

requirements.source_quote: "Create an executive summary outlining important details."
requirements.requirement: An executive summary that a decision-maker can read without opening the rest of the site.
requirements.what_exists: A one-page brief with the headline numbers, the four things that block a decision, what changed in this session, and an explicit list of what is not claimed.
requirements.review: The summary links every claim to the page or official source that supports it; a summary is only as good as those links.

requirements.source_quote: "There should be no manual input on my part. Work on your own to finish all tasks in this session."
requirements.requirement: The session completes the work with no questions, approvals or data entry required from the operator.
requirements.what_exists: All capture, reconciliation, grading, register generation, site build, link checking and PR/merge steps were executed autonomously. Decisions the operator must own are collected in the Suggestions section with a decision field, so they are surfaced rather than blocking.
requirements.what_is_missing: The operator decisions themselves. Those are intentionally left open.
requirements.review: No operator input was requested at any point in this session.

requirements.source_quote: "Create a github page live site for this repo with a clean landing page and subpages organized by category ... include any analysis and findings."
requirements.requirement: A live GitHub Pages site with a landing page, category subpages, and every finding in a table that carries a source link.
requirements.what_exists: The root dashboard is regenerated with the new sections in its navigation, and every requirements page is published under the same origin. Each table row that states a fact carries an official source link; rows that cannot be confirmed are blank and tagged.
requirements.review: Publication is verified by fetching the live URL after the deploy, not by assuming the workflow succeeded.

requirements.source_quote: "Verify line by line. Every table row must have a source link to an official site. If a value can't be confirmed from an official source, leave it blank and flag it as unverified. Never infer or fill in values."
requirements.requirement: Cell-level verification against official sources, with blanks and flags instead of inference.
requirements.what_exists: The strongest available test: the 137-game official game log is recomputed into every club's W-L-T, PCT, PF, PA, NET, HOME and ROAD and compared to the official standings page, giving 352 of 352 cells matching with zero tolerance. The Week 9 scores were transcribed fresh and every derived number is recomputed by script from the transcription rather than typed.
requirements.what_is_missing: Full team-level reconciliation for Weeks 6 to 8 cannot be completed from the standings page alone because the inherited four-game sample gives several clubs only six or seven games; this is stated on the page rather than papered over. Rows whose source was not observed in this session are labelled as inherited, not re-verified.
requirements.review: 352 of 352 is a reconciliation of the arithmetic and the current standings, not a re-reading of all sixteen historical box scores.
